brief: A4 - parity arm + gold: HF DeepSeek-OCR reference (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR and deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2)

views.free_ocr: prompt '<image>\nFree OCR.' - the plain-text mode; this is the CER gate T14 needs
views.grounding_raw: prompt '<image>\n<|grounding|>Convert the document to markdown.' - raw generation, <|ref|>/<|det|> boxes included
views.grounding_doc: the same generation after the checkpoint's own post-processing (infer(save_results=True) -> result.mmd), which drops the box markup and keeps the markdown

repro: # reference run (Kaggle GPU, chr1s4) - the Mac never loads these weights
KAGGLE_API_TOKEN=<chr1s4> python -c "from kaggle import KaggleApi; a=KaggleApi(); a.authenticate(); print(a.kernels_push('tools/kaggle/deepseek-ocr-parity'))"
KAGGLE_API_TOKEN=<chr1s4> python -c "from kaggle import KaggleApi; a=KaggleApi(); a.authenticate(); a.kernels_output('chr1s4/crispembed-deepseek-ocr-reference-parity', path='<dir>', force=True)"
# scoring, offline, from the retrieved transcripts (three views per corpus)
notes: NO TIMING COLUMN HERE IS A LATENCY MEASUREMENT. `generation_s` is wall time for one transformers generate() call on one Kaggle Tesla T4 with eager attention. It is recorded so a page that took 89 s is visible, and for no other purpose. It must never be quoted next to a Mac number or next to the checkpoint's own vLLM throughput.

The request is not a deviation: the checkpoint's own modeling_deepseekocr*.py::infer() runs with the model card's arguments, and the kernel only wraps model.generate to record what infer() built. Prompt, conversation template, crop geometry, image-token accounting and sampling parameters are the checkpoint's code, not a reimplementation.

dtype is NOT a deviation this time. bf16 was probed on the card (matmul, conv2d, SDPA) before use and all three passed on torch 2.10.0+cu128 / sm_75, so the run is the card's bfloat16 and the fp16 fallback path never fired. This differs from the Qwen2.5-VL and olmOCR arms, which recorded fp16.

Attention IS a deviation, and it is forced rather than chosen: the card passes _attn_implementation='flash_attention_2', sm_75 has no FA2, and the checkpoint's ATTENTION_CLASSES dict offers only {eager, flash_attention_2} (plus mla_/mha_ prefixed copies) - there is no sdpa entry to substitute. eager was verified at runtime: config._attn_implementation == 'eager' and the instantiated decoder attention class is LlamaAttention, not LlamaFlashAttention2. The vision towers never used FA2 (v1's ViT is built with use_flash_attn=False, v2's Qwen2 encoder with attn_implementation='sdpa'), so no sdpa-vs-eager A/B applies to them either.

The gold is reproducible: generation_config carries no do_sample, infer() passes temperature=0.0, and a re-run of two pages per checkpoint came back byte-identical (synth_00_blur.png and commons_example_receipt.png, both models). No page needed a retry and no page hit the 240 s stopping criterion except where noted below.

The two checkpoints do not preprocess the same corpus the same way, and the difference is a hardcoded threshold rather than the image: v1 skips cropping when both sides are <= 640, v2 when both are <= 768. commons_example_receipt.png (500x650) therefore gets 6 crops of 640x640 and 903 image tokens under v1 and a single 1024x1024 global view with 257 image tokens under v2. Over the 25 fixtures v1 takes the single-view path 12 times and v2 19 times. Any native lane claiming parity has to reproduce the threshold, not just the preset.

The transformers path the card documents has NO repetition guard equivalent to the one its own vLLM snippet installs. infer() passes no_repeat_ngram_size=20; the vLLM recipe additionally installs NGramPerReqLogitsProcessor with ngram_size=30, window_size=90 and a / whitelist. On simple_form.png the grounding prompt made DeepSeek-OCR emit 2073 tokens of a repeating single-character box list (F/R/E, 6066 raw chars against 247 reference chars, 89.1 s, raw CER 23.38) because each repeat carries different coordinates and so never forms a repeated 20-gram. DeepSeek-OCR-2 degrades on the same page but far less (518 tokens, raw CER 5.41, document-view CER 0.1215).

Three scored views, because one number would hide the difference between misreading a page and formatting it. free_ocr is the plain-text mode and is the CER gate. grounding_raw keeps the <|ref|>/<|det|> box markup the model emits and is dominated by coordinate text - it is a diagnostic only. grounding_doc is the same generation after infer()'s own post-processing (result.mmd), which is what a caller actually receives.

Markup inflates the primary CER even in the plain-OCR mode. On receipt_historical.png DeepSeek-OCR answered 'Free OCR.' with HTML <table> rows: 2202 chars against 768 reference chars, CER 2.0417 while the markup-stripped view is 0.1094. DeepSeek-OCR-2 answered the same page in markdown headings (CER 0.3633, stripped 0.1667). Quote both columns.
`.free_ocr.mmd` is not shipped: infer()'s post-processing is a no-op when the prompt carries no <|grounding|>, verified byte-identical on all 50 plain-mode pages before deletion.

The brief names deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR; src/deepseek_ocr2.cpp loads deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2. Both were run because only the second is a gate for T14 and only the first is what the brief asked for. The native lane's prompt ('\nFree OCR.' after the image tokens, plain template, bos first) matches the free_ocr contract captured here.
